control_results.control_name: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets
control_results.score_rationale: The policy includes general requirements for safeguarding information systems and monitoring environments, but lacks explicit, systematic procedures for inventory and active management of all enterprise assets across physical, virtual, remote, and cloud environments.
evidence: The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment, and will regularly monitor the effectiveness of such safeguards.
Identify systems without which it would be difficult for the business to operate.
Policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.
gaps: No explicit requirement for maintaining a comprehensive, up-to-date inventory of all enterprise assets (including cloud and remote assets).
No defined process for tracking assets, correcting unauthorized assets, or integration with asset management solutions.
No mention of inventory reconciliation, automated asset discovery, or periodic asset reviews.
recommendations: Establish and document procedures for maintaining a detailed, up-to-date inventory of all enterprise assets, including physical, virtual, remote, and cloud assets.
Implement asset tracking and reconciliation mechanisms, including automated tools where possible.
Define periodic review and correction processes for asset inventory to ensure completeness and accuracy.
Integrate asset management processes with risk assessment and security monitoring.

control_results.control_name: Inventory and Control of Software Assets
control_results.score_rationale: The policy contains some relevant controls such as limiting access to software, audit mechanisms, and periodic audits, but lacks comprehensive, formal processes for maintaining an up-to-date inventory of software assets and does not specify mechanisms for detecting or blocking unauthorized/unmanaged software.
evidence: authorized individuals within Provider may monitor equipment, systems and network traffic at any time
Provider reserves the right to audit networks and systems on a periodic basis to ensure compliance and security
procedures to control and validate a person’s access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control, and control of access to software programs for testing and revision

Access control. Technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic Information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted appropriate access rights.
Audit controls. Hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use electronic Information.
gaps: No explicit requirement or process for maintaining a complete and up-to-date inventory of all software installed on the network.
No process defined for the review or approval of software installations.
No stated mechanism for detecting, blocking, or removing unauthorized or unmanaged software.
Does not identify responsible roles for software asset management or specify reporting and accountability.
No mention of periodic review of authorized software or removal of unauthorized software.
recommendations: Implement and formally document a centralized process for maintaining an inventory of all software assets, including versioning and ownership.
Define and enforce a standardized software approval process ensuring only authorized software can be installed or executed.
Adopt technical controls for automated detection and blocking of unauthorized software on endpoints and servers.
Assign clear accountability and reporting responsibilities for software asset management.
Establish procedures for periodic review, verification, and removal of unauthorized or unmanaged software.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy describes formal, documented processes for risk assessment, access controls, encryption, secure handling, and disposal of data. However, data classification and comprehensive data loss prevention (DLP) controls are only implicitly addressed and lack specific procedures or continuous improvement mechanisms.
evidence: The Coordinator will establish procedures for identifying and assessing risks in each relevant area of Provider’s operations.

The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment, and will regularly monitor the effectiveness of such safeguards.
A mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic Information.
Procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic Information.
Procedures to restore any loss of data.
Improper Disposal Procedures – Improper disposal procedures may allow a third party to steal or access data, reconstruct data, or commit ‘dumpster diving.’
Installation of firewalls, restricted access, data encryption, or limited network/internet access are all possible safeguards in this example.
gaps: No explicit policy on identifying and classifying data according to sensitivity or regulatory requirements.
Data loss prevention (DLP) tools and controls are not specifically mentioned or mandated.
Documented process for secure data retention and disposal is not sufficiently detailed.
No evidence of metrics or continuous improvement/cycle for data protection controls.
recommendations: Develop and implement a formal process for data identification and classification, specifying categories based on sensitivity and regulatory requirements.
Document and mandate the use of data loss prevention (DLP) technologies and controls for both endpoint and network data protection.
Establish clear, detailed procedures for secure data retention and disposal, including requirements for shredding, wiping, or destruction based on data classification.
Define metrics to monitor effectiveness of data protection controls and require periodic review and update as part of risk management.

control_results.control_name: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software
control_results.score_rationale: The policy contains several elements related to risk assessment, system auditing, and technical safeguards, but it does not explicitly reference secure configuration baselines, hardening guides, or formal configuration management processes for assets and software as required by CIS-4.
evidence: Provider reserves the right to audit networks and systems on a periodic basis to ensure compliance and security.

The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment, and will regularly monitor the effectiveness of such safeguards.
Software installs to reduce the risk of introducing a security risk via an installed program (such as an imbedded virus or Trojan).
gaps: No mention of using hardening guides (such as CIS Benchmarks or vendor best practices) for secure baseline configurations.
No requirement for establishing and documenting secure configuration standards for hardware and software.
No formal configuration management process described for maintaining or monitoring configurations over time.
No reference to remediation of non-compliant configurations or integration with vulnerability management.
recommendations: Establish and document secure configuration baselines for all enterprise assets and critical software, referencing industry hardening guides (e.g., CIS Benchmarks, NIST, vendor recommendations).
Implement a formal configuration management process, including version control, monitoring for drift, and regular review of configuration settings.
Document procedures for applying, testing, and maintaining secure configurations, and integrate these with vulnerability management and asset inventory processes.
Define clear accountability for configuration management tasks and establish metrics for compliance with secure baselines.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy provides formal, documented processes for authorization, account management, and access review, covering most requirements for user, admin, and service accounts, but lacks explicit detail about tooling, periodic reviews, and metrics for accountability.
evidence: Policies and procedures that, based upon the entity’s access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user’s right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.

Workforce security. Policies and procedures to ensure that all company employees have appropriate access to electronic Information and to prevent any unauthorized company employees from obtaining access to electronic Information.
Procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of company employees who work with electronic Information or in locations where it might be accessed;
Policies and procedures for granting access to electronic Information, for example, through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.

Technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic Information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted appropriate access rights.
A unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
gaps: No mention of specific tools used for account management or automation.
No explicit reference to managing service accounts or administrator accounts distinctly.
No evidence of periodic review or monitoring of account management effectiveness.
Lacks details on metrics and accountability for measuring access control effectiveness.
recommendations: Explicitly document procedures for managing administrator and service accounts, including assignment, monitoring, and reviews.
Specify tools and automation used for account provisioning, deprovisioning, and access management.
Add requirements for periodic reviews of access rights and account management practices, including regular audits.
Define accountability and metrics for measuring the effectiveness of account management and access controls.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy defines and documents formal processes for access authorization, modification, review, and revocation for user accounts, including administrators, workforce, and service contexts. However, it lacks explicit references to technical automation, in-depth metrics, and continuous measurement or improvement practices.
evidence: Policies and procedures for granting access to electronic Information, for example, through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.

Policies and procedures that, based upon the entity’s access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user’s right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.
Procedures for terminating access to electronic Information under appropriate circumstances, such as, for example, when the employment of a company employee ends.

Technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic Information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted appropriate access rights.
gaps: No explicit mention of tools or automation for provisioning, reviewing, or revoking access credentials.
No reference to measurement, monitoring, or accountability using defined metrics.
No articulation of continuous improvement processes.
Limited explicit coverage of service accounts and administrator privileges as opposed to general user accounts.
recommendations: Incorporate explicit requirements for using automated tools to manage and audit access credentials, including for administrator and service accounts.
Define and implement metrics to routinely monitor access control processes and outcomes, assigning clear accountability.
Establish processes for periodic review and continuous improvement of access control practices.
Clearly distinguish requirements and procedures for user, administrator, and service account management throughout the policy.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy demonstrates defined, formal processes for periodic risk assessment and monitoring safeguards, and includes requirements for patch management and scanning, but lacks explicit language on continuous vulnerability tracking, centralized reporting, remediation prioritization, and metric-based evaluation.
evidence: The Coordinator will review the Program annually to ensure ongoing compliance, as well as consistency with other existing and future laws and regulations. The Coordinator will provide periodic reports on the status of the Program and note any changes to the overall risk assessment and changes to established safeguards.
Ensure that patches are current.
Upgrade any unsupported operating systems for desktops and servers.
Scan and filter incoming emails and files that could contain viruses.
An accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic Information.
Security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
Performance of periodic technical and nontechnical evaluations in response to any environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic Information.
gaps: No explicit mention of continuous vulnerability scanning or use of automated tools.
No formal process for tracking vulnerabilities across all enterprise assets on an ongoing basis.
No defined prioritization process for remediation activities based on risk or exposure.
No requirement for centralized vulnerability reporting or metrics to measure remediation or minimize attacker window.
Remediation plans and timeframes are not articulated; focus is on periodic review rather than continuous assessment.
recommendations: Implement a formal, documented vulnerability management process that includes continuous or frequent automated scanning of all enterprise assets.
Establish centralized tracking of vulnerabilities, including assigned responsibility and remediation timeframes.
Adopt risk-based prioritization for vulnerability remediation based on asset criticality and threat intelligence.
Define metrics for vulnerability management efficiency (e.g., mean time to remediation, percentage of assets scanned, etc.) and monitor them regularly.
Integrate vulnerability management with risk assessment and incident response processes for end-to-end coverage.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy includes documented processes for audit controls, periodic log review, and procedures to monitor and examine system activity, but lacks clear detail on alerting, log retention durations, defined metrics, and continuous improvement.
evidence: Audit controls. Hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use electronic Information.
Procedures to regularly review records of Information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.
Security management process. Policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment, and will regularly monitor the effectiveness of such safeguards.
gaps: No explicit requirement to collect all relevant security events or specify which events must be logged.
No mention of real-time alerting on suspicious or critical events in audit logs.
No defined minimum or maximum retention periods for audit logs.
No evidence of log review frequency, metrics, or accountability.
No process for continual improvement or integration with wider risk management after periodic review.
recommendations: Specify which types of events must be logged and ensure comprehensive collection across relevant systems.
Formally require real-time alerting on significant log events (e.g., potential intrusions, failures).
Define and document audit log retention periods consistent with regulatory and risk requirements.
Set clear responsibilities, accountability, and frequency for log reviews with metrics for effectiveness.
Integrate audit log management review with the organization's risk management and continual improvement processes.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy demonstrates a formal, documented approach to email and web browser protections through several explicit safeguards and user requirements, but lacks details on metrics, consistent operational procedures, or continuous improvement mechanisms across all elements of the control.
evidence: Scan and filter incoming emails and files that could contain viruses.
erface for information contained on Internet / Intranet / Extranet-related systems should be classified as either confidential or not confidential...
All hosts ... shall be continually executing approved virus-scanning software with a current virus database.
Employees must use extreme caution when opening e-mail attachments received from unknown senders, which may contain viruses, e-mail bombs, or Trojan horse code.

Security awareness and training. A security awareness and training program for all company employees (including management). This safeguard may be implemented by establishment of periodic security updates, procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software...
Security management process. Policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.
gaps: No mention of web browser-specific security configurations or controls (e.g., restricting use of plugins, controlling active content, blocking malicious/reputation-based URLs).
Lacks specifics on automated detection and alerting of phishing or compromised web/email traffic.
No metrics or measures to assess effectiveness of email and web browser controls.

recommendations: Define and implement web browser security baseline configurations (e.g., prevent installation of unapproved plugins, block malicious URLs, manage scripting).
Establish and document processes for automated detection and alerting on email/web-based threats (phishing, malware).
Develop and monitor metrics for the effectiveness of email and web browser protections.
Specify regular reviews for control effectiveness and integrate with risk management/continuous improvement processes.
Document and implement the use of sandboxing or isolation techniques for email attachments and untrusted web content.
Explicitly require anti-malware/anti-phishing tools and controls for web browsers, not just general anti-virus.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy includes several malware defense elements such as email/file scanning, patch management, user training, and periodic evaluations, indicating a formal and documented process. However, detail is lacking on the use of automated tools for malware prevention and measurement of effectiveness.
evidence: Scan and filter incoming emails and files that could contain viruses.
Ensure that patches are current.
Upgrade any unsupported operating systems for desktops and servers.
Security awareness and training program for all company employees ... including procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software.

The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment, and will regularly monitor the effectiveness of such safeguards.
gaps: No explicit requirement to deploy automated anti-malware tools on all enterprise assets.
Limited mention of controlling the spread and execution of malicious code (e.g., application whitelisting, execution restriction).

control_results.score_rationale: The policy formally recognizes the need for backup, restoration, contingency planning, and includes periodic testing and evaluation, but lacks detail on established frequency, metrics, and systematic improvement processes.
evidence: Procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic Information.
Procedures to restore any loss of data.
Procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.
Performance of periodic technical and nontechnical evaluations in response to any environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic Information.

Policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (for example, fire, vandalism, system failure, and natural disaster) that damages systems that contain electronic Information. control_results.score_rationale: The policy references general technical safeguards, restricting network privileges, and risk-based implementation but lacks explicit requirements for secure network configuration, documentation of diagrams, segmentation, or protocol hardening. No evidence of detailed network management procedures or configuration baselines is provided.
evidence: "The Coordinator will design, implement, and maintain in writing, the administrative, technical, and physical safeguards necessary to control the risks identified through risk assessment…" (Excerpt 1)

"Restrict network administrative privileges. Computer networks rely on a hierarchical system of access levels to help protect critical parts of the network from both accidental and intentional alterations." (Excerpt 3)
"Ensure that patches are current." (Excerpt 3)
gaps: No mention of maintaining or updating network diagrams or topologies.
No formal process for secure baseline configuration of network infrastructure assets.
No explicit reference to network segmentation practices.
Secure protocols (e.g., disabling insecure protocols, enforcing encryption) are not addressed.
No evidence of monitoring, metrics, or continuous improvement specific to network management.
recommendations: Develop and mandate documented processes for configuring network infrastructure securely, including specifying configuration baselines.
Require and maintain up-to-date network diagrams to support management and incident response.
Implement and document network segmentation practices aligned to data sensitivity and business needs.
Define requirements for use of secure network protocols (e.g., SSH, TLS) and disallow insecure legacy protocols.
Establish regular reviews, monitoring, and audits of network configurations with defined accountability metrics.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy formally documents network monitoring and defense activities, including assigning responsibility, conducting periodic reviews, and allowing network monitoring and audits. control_results.score_rationale: The policy establishes a formal security awareness and training program, mandates periodic updates, and assigns responsibility, but lacks details on ongoing behavior measurement, specific metrics, continuous improvement, and integration with risk management processes.
evidence: A security awareness and training program for all company employees (including management). This safeguard may be implemented by establishment of periodic security updates, procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software, procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies, and/or procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.
The Coordinator will prepare and maintain written safeguards and will provide guidance on implementation of safeguards to all affected company employees.
The Coordinator will be responsible for ensuring that company staff is trained in the relevant legal requirements for handling and storing Information.
Employee Training: All employees that have access to Information or work with systems that handle Information should receive adequate training for handling and disposal of such Information.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy documents refer to departmental risk assessments and periodic reviews, but lack a formal, documented process specifically for evaluating service providers' controls over sensitive data and critical platforms.
